story_description: Implement a persistent SQLite cache layer for registry data that stores fetched skills, plugins, and agents locally with time-to-live expiration to reduce network requests, enable offline access, and provide fast startup times for the registry UI.
task_description: Create the SQLite-backed cache implementation with 24-hour TTL expiration, CRUD operations for registry items, cache invalidation logic, and migration support for schema evolution.
atom_description: Implement RegistryCache actor in Blaze/Sources/Registry/RegistryCache.swift providing SQLite-backed persistence for RegistryResponse data with 24-hour TTL expiration. The cache stores skills, plugins, and agents in normalized tables with foreign keys, supports atomic batch inserts, provides staleness checks via lastUpdated timestamps, implements cache invalidation on TTL expiry or manual refresh, and handles schema migrations for future changes. Uses SQLite.swift library for type-safe database operations.
problem_statement: The registry fetcher makes network requests to retrieve skills, plugins, and agents from remote sources. Without local caching, every app launch or UI refresh triggers network traffic, causes startup latency, and fails completely when offline. A SQLite cache with TTL expiration provides fast local reads, reduces API load, enables offline functionality, and maintains freshness through periodic re-validation.

functional_requirements: FR-01: RegistryCache must initialize database schema on first access, creating all tables if not exists
FR-02: cacheResponse must atomically replace all cached items in a single transaction
FR-03: getCachedResponse must return nil if cache is empty or corrupted, not throw
FR-04: isCacheValid must return false if lastFetched is older than 24 hours
FR-05: isCacheValid must return false if cacheVersion does not match current schema version
FR-06: invalidateCache must delete all rows from skills, plugins, agents tables and reset metadata
FR-07: Cache must store configSchema as JSON TEXT column preserving nested structure
FR-08: Cache must store requiredSkills as JSON array TEXT column
FR-09: Cache must store forCli as JSON array TEXT column for each item type
FR-10: getCacheStats must return item counts, database file size, and lastFetched timestamp
FR-11: Database file path must be configurable for testing with in-memory or temp file options
FR-12: Schema migration must run automatically on app launch if cacheVersion is outdated
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-01: getCachedResponse must complete in under 50ms for 1000 total items
NFR-02: cacheResponse must complete in under 200ms for 1000 total items using batch insert
NFR-03: Database file size must not exceed 10MB for 1000 items with typical metadata
NFR-04: Cache operations must not block UI thread (enforced by actor isolation)
NFR-05: Must handle concurrent read/write requests without data corruption
NFR-06: Must log cache hits/misses for observability

edge_cases: Empty cache on first launch returns nil from getCachedResponse without error
Corrupted database file triggers automatic rebuild from scratch
Missing Application Support directory is created automatically
Partial write failure rolls back transaction leaving cache in previous state
Concurrent reads during write operation are serialized by actor
Database locked by another process throws RegistryCacheError.readFailed
Zero items in response clears cache (valid empty registry state)
Very large configSchema JSON (over 1MB) stores successfully
Unicode characters in item names and descriptions preserve correctly
Future schema version in database triggers migration or rebuild
lastFetched exactly 24 hours old is considered expired (exclusive boundary)
Nil optional fields in RegistryMetadata encode as JSON null
failure_modes: Database file permissions denied - throw RegistryCacheError.databaseNotFound
Disk full during write - throw RegistryCacheError.writeFailed, transaction rolled back
JSON encoding failure for complex configSchema - throw RegistryCacheError.writeFailed
JSON decoding failure for malformed stored data - return nil from getCachedResponse (rebuild on next fetch)
Schema migration failure - throw RegistryCacheError.migrationFailed, app shows error and offers reset
SQLite.swift library not available - compile error caught at build time
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Registry/RegistryCache.swift and Tests/RegistryCacheTests.swift. Remove SQLite.swift dependency from Package.swift if not used elsewhere. User data in registry_cache.db is transient cache only - no user data loss. Coordinator falls back to always fetching from network.

open_questions: Should TTL be configurable via UserDefaults or hardcoded to 24h for simplicity?
Should cache store raw JSON blob or normalized tables for query flexibility?
Should cache support partial updates or only full replacement?
Is SQLite.swift the right choice or should we use GRDB.swift for better Swift integration?
notes: The cache is the performance foundation for the registry system. Fast cache reads enable instant UI display on app launch. The 24h TTL balances freshness with API rate limits. Schema migration support future-proofs the design for registry schema changes without forcing users to clear cache manually.

risks: SQLite.swift dependency may have version conflicts with other packages
Database corruption from app crash during write could lose cache
Performance may degrade with very large registry over 10000 items
Schema migration bugs could corrupt existing cache data
Actor isolation overhead may impact performance for high-frequency access
mitigations: Pin SQLite.swift to specific version and test compatibility before merging
Use SQLite transactions for atomic writes that rollback on failure
Add pagination or lazy loading if item counts exceed 10000
Comprehensive migration tests with fixtures for each schema version
Batch operations and connection pooling if actor overhead becomes measurable
risk_register.blast_radius: Medium - cache failure falls back to network fetch, but impacts startup performance and offline capability. No user data loss since cache is transient.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If cache implementation proves problematic, coordinator can bypass cache and always fetch from network. Users experience slower startup but full functionality. Cache can be deleted and rebuilt at any time.
